title: Brainstem and cerebellum anatomy
description: Locate brainstem levels, cranial-nerve nuclei, pyramids and cerebellar peduncles, cortex and nuclei.

questions.question: What are the three parts of the brainstem?
questions.answer: The brainstem consists of midbrain, pons and medulla. It carries major pathways and houses many cranial-nerve nuclei.

questions.question: What does the cerebellum do?
questions.answer: The cerebellum helps coordinate movement, timing and balance by integrating sensory and motor information; it is not the same structure as the brainstem.

questions.question: What is the midbrain?
questions.answer: Rostral brainstem around cerebral aqueduct between diencephalon and pons. Function: Hosts III/IV-related nuclei and visual/auditory orienting circuits.

questions.question: Where is the inferior colliculus located?
questions.answer: Dorsal caudal midbrain auditory relay structure. Function: Integrates auditory pathway toward thalamus.

questions.question: What is the function of the cerebral peduncles?
questions.answer: Function: Transmit corticospinal, corticobulbar and corticopontine signals. Ventral midbrain bundles carrying major descending cortical fibers.
